title: Preservation of Scripture
definition: The preservation of Scripture means that God faithfully keeps His Word so that His people are not left without His true testimony.
summary: The Lord who gave His Word also guards its witness, ensuring that His people may hear, read, teach, and obey what He has spoken.
christFocus: Christ taught that Scripture cannot be broken and that God's Word endures, giving confidence that His promises remain sure.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content: Preservation of Scripture teaches that God's people must receive this truth under the authority of the Lord, allowing Scripture itself to define the doctrine rather than personal opinion, tradition, or culture.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This doctrine matters because it protects the believer from confusion and helps the church remain anchored in what God has actually spoken. Without this truth, faith can drift toward feelings, assumptions, or human wisdom.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: A disciple should respond to preservation of scripture by reading the Word prayerfully, testing beliefs by Scripture, obeying what God reveals, and helping others handle the Bible with humility, clarity, and faith.

studySections.heading: Guardrails and Common Errors
studySections.content: This doctrine should not be used to win arguments while neglecting love, nor should it be separated from prayer, obedience, and dependence on the Holy Spirit. The goal is faithful submission to God, not mere possession of information.

sources: Scripture references listed in this doctrine entry.
